mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated rates compress equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of more than 0.2 percentage points over the past month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in reduced economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 1 month over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that may lead to wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, which subsequently causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 3.5%) does not produce negative returns: when both conditions hold, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a slowdown.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, HOUST below 1400 thousand units is not associated with negative 20-day forward returns: the average return is positive or not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (relative to 2017=100) signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the average 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals weakening residential demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1400, the average 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market that may accelerate inflation, leading the Federal Reserve to raise rates, which subsequently causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), a declining UNRATE is not associated with negative 5-day forward returns: the average return is positive or not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising rapidly and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is not rising in response, it signals a failure of monetary policy to control inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors fear stagflation.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (CPIAUCSL rising > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS not rising) does not produce negative returns: when both conditions hold, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
